questions.q: What is the main deliverable this lab asks you to produce?
options: A one-page, five-row multi-cloud governance control map pairing each primary-cloud control with its secondary-cloud equivalent and an owner
A fully deployed AWS account with live IAM roles
A 50-page governance policy document
A certification exam administered by Microsoft and AWS jointly
questions.explain: The lab is explicitly designed to not require a live subscription — it's a one-page control map covering identity, storage, catalog, policy enforcement, and audit logging.

questions.q: In the lab's example AWS trust policy snippet, what is the purpose of the 'sts:ExternalId' condition?
options: It gates the role so only a party that also knows the shared External ID secret can assume it, not just anyone who knows the trusted account ID
It sets the maximum number of AWS users allowed in the account
It defines the AWS region where the role can be used
It has no real security purpose and is optional decoration
questions.explain: This mirrors the federated role trust pattern from Lesson 22 — the External ID is a shared secret that prevents anyone who merely learns the account ID from assuming the role.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what column does the lab say most real-world control maps skip, and why does it matter?
options: An 'owner' column naming who is responsible for keeping both sides of each row in sync — without it, there's no one accountable for catching drift
A column listing the exact dollar cost of each cloud service
A column listing the company's stock ticker symbol
A column counting the total number of employees at the company
questions.explain: An honestly 'unassigned' owner is more useful than a map that looks complete but isn't backed by anyone's actual responsibility.

questions.q: What does the lab's Step 5 self-check ask you to evaluate for each row of your control map?
options: Whether the secondary-cloud control would update automatically if the primary-cloud control changed, or whether someone would have to remember to update it by hand
Whether the row uses more than ten words
Whether the company has more Azure employees than AWS employees
Whether the control map was approved by a government regulator
questions.explain: Any row that depends on someone remembering to update it by hand is, per Lesson 21, a policy-drift risk — the self-check surfaces exactly where drift is most likely to happen.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why is a finished control map a legitimate artifact to bring to a real governance job interview?
options: It shows you understand both clouds' native governance tools well enough to translate between them, not just memorize one
It proves you have an active AWS and Azure certification
It guarantees you will pass any technical interview automatically
It is a legally binding compliance document
questions.explain: The lab frames the control map as evidence of practical, cross-cloud governance thinking — exactly the skill a multi-cloud governance role requires.
